cefrAlignment: C1: choosing the right kind of support (hypothetical example, anecdote, analogy, counter-example) and linking it back matches the C1 descriptors for supporting points with relevant examples in sustained discourse; the language (a case in point, it just goes to show, counter-example) is C1.
examFidelity: IELTS Part 3 (no prep, 60 s) and TOEFL Take an Interview (no prep, 45 s, early experience-type question) match exams.ts and its description of early versus later interview questions.
fixes: Trimmed the TOEFL model (ex5) from 108 to 99 words; at 108 words it needed about 145 wpm to fit 45 s
Changed the last sentence in the ex3 ordering task from a fragment starting 'Which just goes to show…' to the full sentence 'That just goes to show…'
learnerOutcome: A learner can back up abstract Part 3 claims with a brief, relevant example, anecdote or analogy and link it back to the question, instead of drifting into long stories or invented statistics.
